literal: By virtue that which comes indeed is happiness; other all are external, fame also do not have.
translation: Only that pleasure which flows from a life of virtue is true happiness; all other pleasures are external to it and yield no lasting praise.
modern: அறவழியில் வருவதே உண்மையான இன்பம் ஆகும்; மற்ற வழிகளில் வருவன எல்லாம் இன்பத்திற்குப் புறம்பானவை, அவை புகழையும் தராது.
explanation: This couplet defines the true source of happiness as virtue. It asserts that only the joy arising from righteous living is genuine and wholesome. Any other form of pleasure obtained through unrighteous means is described as external, meaning it is superficial, fleeting, and disconnected from the soul. Furthermore, such pleasures do not bring any true or lasting glory to a person.
